purpose: CURRENT-STATE.json is the single place for the MicroDuck robot's CURRENT measured facts. Sim judgements, briefs and child sessions read these values from here. History (memory files, DECISIONS.md, logs, transcripts, code comments) explains how a value was reached and is never a source for the current value. When a measurement changes a fact, update its entry here in the same turn and move the old value into its 'superseded' list.

servo_read_drop_fraction.meaning: Fraction of 20 ms walk-mode ticks without a fresh servo sync read while the legs step (the policy skips those ticks and the servos hold the last goals).
servo_read_drop_fraction.source: 2026-10-31 A7Z brain logs (slices /tmp/t1-robot/163444.jsonl, 163517.jsonl on the Mac): walk 1 16:34:36 17 % stale reads, walk 2 16:35:17 78 % (most after the fall began); standing afterwards 12-22 % (walk61 brain at 16:37 included). Mostly whole frames (all 14 servos missing at once); sync read p50 18.4 ms instead of 9.3, max 48-75 ms; the brain's own compute per tick 6-7 ms, unchanged. Before: 10/30 21:24-21:26 walks 0-3 %, read p50 9.3 ms, and 10/31 16:31-16:33:20 on the battery 0-3.6 %. Onset 16:33:30 EDT, the second the head touch bus (TWI0 2510000.twi, XIAO 0x2a) locked up: about 100 kernel error lines per s from then on (b0052 kmsg), IMU 193 -> 75 samples/s, whole-frame servo misses whose replies never arrive (lost, not late). The same touch fault happened on 10/30 about 21:29 on the bench supply. Likely path (inference): the error flood printed to the 115200 serial console at console loglevel 4 plus the touch driver's busy-waits delays interrupts, and the DMA-less servo UART ttyAS2 drops bytes. A fault state, not a steady value: a fresh boot reads at the old rate until the touch bus locks up again. After the battery-swap boot (b0053, 16:58): 0 % stale in 500 standing ticks at 17:13, read p50 9.4 ms, 47.5 Hz, touch bus not jammed. Fixes deployed 17:12 (cc0593d7: parser length and CRC checks, touch back-off, console loglevel 1, supply auto); they load at the next brain start. Controlled check 17:20 (b0053): the touch bus jammed again at about 17:20 (about 145 kernel error lines per s, worse than 16:33) with console loglevel 1 live and the OLD brain code still running; standing in walk mode at zero command it read 47.2-47.5 Hz, 3 of 1500 ticks missing, IMU 182-196 samples/s. So the console printing was the starving path; stepping ticks under a jam are not measured yet.

a7z_imu_bus.meaning: How the A7Z reaches the IMU. In drv mode (twi_drv_used = 1, set by Radxa's sun60iw2p1-twi7.dtbo) TWI7 wedges after boot, after zero-length writes and after reads that hit the IMU while it resets, until the driver is rebound. The engine overlay must load after Radxa's twi7 overlay; u-boot-update (run by rsetup on every overlay change) orders /boot/dtbo alphabetically, hence the zz- name.

ankle_bend_stall.value: In the held bend (groundpick phase 0.33) both ankles stop at about 1.25 rad (-1.246, +1.259) with their goals on the 1.571 rad clamp, 0.32 rad of held error; the sim's ankles reach 1.37-1.43 with 0.07-0.11 rad. A 1.25 rad ankle limit in the sim closes the bend trunk gap (-4.6 to +0.3 deg) and the camera height (23.9 to 15.6 mm, scan 14.5). The cable sits in the rear socket of both ankle servos; in the bend that socket faces the foot, its plug is 0.6 mm from the foot at 1.25 rad in the model, and the bend scan shows the cable running into that crease on both ankles. The front socket is empty and faces up (plug 3.4 mm from the foot through 1.571 rad). Without the plug the servo case meets the foot at about 1.35-1.40 rad. Plug as the stop is model plus scan, not yet proven by moving it.
ankle_bend_stall.meaning: Why the sim chain and the robot part ways in the bend, and what the groundpick policy's ankle goal does on this robot. The as-built sim and training routes stop the ankle at the model's heel contact, 1.36 rad (D-040); until the cable moves to the front socket the robot stops earlier than the sim.
